name: Ilango Adigal
bio: Ilango Adigal (இளங்கோ அடிகள், “the revered prince Ilango”) is the traditional author of the Silappatikaram (“The Tale of the Anklet”), the earliest of Tamil's great epics. Tradition makes him a prince of the Chera dynasty, a brother of the king Senguttuvan, who gave up the throne to become a Jain ascetic; the epic's own prologue speaks of him in that character, living in retirement at Kunavayil. Nothing else about his life is documented, and his date is debated; the fifth or sixth century CE is a common scholarly estimate.

The Silappatikaram tells how the merchant Kovalan leaves his wife Kannagi for the dancer Madhavi, returns to Kannagi, and goes with her to Madurai to sell one of her anklets, where he is wrongly put to death by the Pandya king. Kannagi proves his innocence and burns the city with the power of her chastity, and she is later honoured as a goddess. The work is in three books (kandams), Pukar, Madurai and Vanji, named for the three Tamil capitals, and in thirty cantos (kathais) that mix several verse metres and song forms with passages of rhythmic prose.
